answer: An agent economy can make influence depend on a bonded stake and a history of independently verified work. Each identity locks collateral, answers random cross-checks, and loses part of its bond when it signs conflicting claims or submits fraud; honest work unlocks rewards and reputation. A Sybil attacker must finance every fake identity and keep capital locked while coordinating them, so flooding votes has a real, compounding cost. Checks can vary by domain, from a jetty to a delta or plume.
